# File paths for all source CSV files
source_files = {
    "Source6_51_0": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_51/training_0.csv",
    "Source6_51_1": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_51/training_1.csv",

    "Source6_51_5": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_51/training_5.csv",
    "Source6_51_6": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_51/training_6.csv",
}

# Step 1: Load all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source_files["Source6_51_0"], index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'batsman_runs'] (516 rows)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source_files["Source6_51_1"], index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'total_runs'] (516 rows)
df2 = pd.read_csv(source_files["Source6_51_2"], index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'batsman_runs'] (258 rows)
df3 = pd.read_csv(source_files["Source6_51_3"], index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'batsman_runs'] (516 rows)
df4 = pd.read_csv(source_files["Source6_51_4"], index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'total_runs'] (516 rows)
df5 = pd.read_csv(source_files["Source6_51_5"], index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'batsman_runs'] (516 rows)
df6 = pd.read_csv(source_files["Source6_51_6"], index_col=0)  # ['batsman', 'no of balls', 'batsman_runs', 'strike'] (516 rows)

# Step 2: Analyze schemas and target columns
# Target columns:
# ['batsman': string,
#  'batsman_runs_x': float,
#  'total_runs_x': integer,
#  'total_runs_y': integer,
#  'batsman_runs_y': integer,
#  'batsman_runs_x_5': integer,
#  'no of balls': integer,
#  'batsman_runs_y_7': integer,
#  'strike': float,
#  'batsman_runs': integer]

# Step 3: Identify how source tables map to target columns:
# - batsman: key column, present in all sources
# - batsman_runs_x: float, from Source6_51_2 (258 rows, batsman_runs float)
# - total_runs_x: integer, from Source6_51_1 (total_runs)
# - total_runs_y: integer, from Source6_51_4 (total_runs)
# - batsman_runs_y: integer, from Source6_51_0 (batsman_runs integer)
# - batsman_runs_x_5: integer, from Source6_51_5 (batsman_runs integer)
# - no of balls: integer, from Source6_51_6
# - batsman_runs_y_7: integer, from Source6_51_3 (batsman_runs integer)
# - strike: float, from Source6_51_6
# - batsman_runs: integer, from Source6_51_0 (batsman_runs integer) or possibly from df0 or df5 or df3, but target examples show batsman_runs as integer, so we take from df0 (Source6_51_0)

# Step 4: Rename columns in each source to match target columns before join
# We will join all on 'batsman' key.

# Rename df2 batsman_runs -> batsman_runs_x (float)
df2_renamed = df2.rename(columns={"batsman_runs": "batsman_runs_x"})

# Rename df1 total_runs -> total_runs_x (int)
df1_renamed = df1.rename(columns={"total_runs": "total_runs_x"})

# Rename df4 total_runs -> total_runs_y (int)
df4_renamed = df4.rename(columns={"total_runs": "total_runs_y"})

# Rename df0 batsman_runs -> batsman_runs_y (int)
df0_renamed = df0.rename(columns={"batsman_runs": "batsman_runs_y"})

# Rename df5 batsman_runs -> batsman_runs_x_5 (int)
df5_renamed = df5.rename(columns={"batsman_runs": "batsman_runs_x_5"})

# df6 already has 'no of balls', 'batsman_runs', 'strike' columns
# Rename df3 batsman_runs -> batsman_runs_y_7 (int)
df3_renamed = df3.rename(columns={"batsman_runs": "batsman_runs_y_7"})

# Step 5: Merge all dataframes on 'batsman' using left joins progressively
# Start from df2_renamed (258 rows) because target examples have 258 rows, so this is the base

df_merge = df2_renamed.copy()

# Join df1_renamed (total_runs_x)
df_merge = df_merge.merge(df1_renamed, on="batsman", how="left")

# Join df4_renamed (total_runs_y)
df_merge = df_merge.merge(df4_renamed, on="batsman", how="left")

# Join df0_renamed (batsman_runs_y)
df_merge = df_merge.merge(df0_renamed, on="batsman", how="left")

# Join df5_renamed (batsman_runs_x_5)
df_merge = df_merge.merge(df5_renamed, on="batsman", how="left")

# Join df6 (no of balls, batsman_runs, strike)
df_merge = df_merge.merge(df6, on="batsman", how="left")

# Join df3_renamed (batsman_runs_y_7)
df_merge = df_merge.merge(df3_renamed, on="batsman", how="left")

# Step 6: Ensure correct dtypes as per target schema
# Target schema types:
# batsman: string
df_merge["batsman"] = df_merge["batsman"].astype(str)

# batsman_runs_x: float
df_merge["batsman_runs_x"] = df_merge["batsman_runs_x"].astype(float)

# total_runs_x: integer (fill NaN with 0 before converting)
df_merge["total_runs_x"] = df_merge["total_runs_x"].fillna(0).astype(int)

# total_runs_y: integer
df_merge["total_runs_y"] = df_merge["total_runs_y"].fillna(0).astype(int)

# batsman_runs_y: integer
df_merge["batsman_runs_y"] = df_merge["batsman_runs_y"].fillna(0).astype(int)

# batsman_runs_x_5: integer
df_merge["batsman_runs_x_5"] = df_merge["batsman_runs_x_5"].fillna(0).astype(int)

# no of balls: integer
df_merge["no of balls"] = df_merge["no of balls"].fillna(0).astype(int)

# batsman_runs_y_7: integer
df_merge["batsman_runs_y_7"] = df_merge["batsman_runs_y_7"].fillna(0).astype(int)

# strike: float
df_merge["strike"] = df_merge["strike"].fillna(0).astype(float)

# batsman_runs: integer (from df6)
df_merge["batsman_runs"] = df_merge["batsman_runs"].fillna(0).astype(int)

# Step 7: Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
target_columns = [
    "batsman",
    "batsman_runs_x",
    "total_runs_x",
    "total_runs_y",
    "batsman_runs_y",
    "batsman_runs_x_5",
    "no of balls",
    "batsman_runs_y_7",
    "strike",
    "batsman_runs",
]

df_final = df_merge[target_columns]

# Step 8: Write the final dataframe to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_51/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_final.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

# Rename columns accordingly:
result = result.rename(columns={
    'batsman_runs_x': 'batsman_runs_x',  # from s0
    'total_runs_x': 'total_runs_x',      # from s1
    'total_runs_y': 'total_runs_y',      # from s4
